title: Choucroute Garnie
subtitle: Alsatian sauerkraut braised with pork and sausages
excerpt: Alsace's signature dish: sauerkraut slow-braised in white wine and goose fat with juniper, caraway, and bay, layered with smoked pork, bacon, and sausages and cooked until the meat is melting and the sauerkraut has drunk up all the flavour around it.

recipe.sourceNotes: Choucroute garnie (garnished sauerkraut) is the central dish of Alsatian cuisine, a region that has been alternately French and German in political terms since the seventeenth century, giving it a cooking tradition that is neither purely one nor the other. The dish is simply sauerkraut (fermented cabbage, choucroute in French, from the German Sauerkraut) braised with white wine and pork products and served with potatoes. What makes it Alsatian is the specific combination: dry Riesling or other Alsatian white wine, juniper berries, caraway seeds, and a variety of pork cuts including smoked pork belly, sausages, and sometimes ham knuckle. It is a generous, convivial dish typically served at the table from the pot.

content.text: Rinse the sauerkraut thoroughly in cold water and squeeze out as much liquid as possible; commercial sauerkraut is often very acidic and salty, and the rinse brings the flavour into balance. Add the sausages and other quick-cooking items in the last 20 minutes only or they will dry out.

items.preparation: smoked; in a thick slab or cut into lardons
German-style pork sausages such as Frankfurters or Bratwurst
smoked gammon joint or ham hock
peeled and halved; to serve alongside

content.text: Heat the duck fat in a large, heavy casserole. Cook the onion and bacon over medium heat for 8 minutes until the onion is soft and the bacon is beginning to colour. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add the rinsed sauerkraut, bay leaves, caraway seeds, and peppercorns. Nestle the ham or gammon among the sauerkraut. Pour in the wine and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly, and braise over low heat or in the oven at 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3 for 1 hour.

Add the sausages, tucking them into the sauerkraut. Cook for a further 25 to 30 minutes. Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Serve everything together at the table: sauerkraut, pork products, and potatoes with Dijon mustard alongside.
